units.title: Fashion
units.intro: Grammar: am/is/are + -ing for actions going on around now, confusing word pairs (accept/except, adapt/adopt), and have/has been + -ing (present perfect continuous) for actions from the past up to now.

lessons.title: Present continuous for a period of time

cards.title: Present continuous for a period of time
rule: **am / is / are + -ing** is for actions happening **now**, and also for actions going on **around now**, over a period: *this week, this month, this year, these days*: *My bicycle is broken, so I **am walking** to school this week.*
It also shows a **change that is happening**: *Fashion **is becoming** more expensive in Asmara.*
Textbook example (Lesson 8.13): *Currently, I’**m attending** a three-month programme in secretarial science.* The writer is not in class now; the course goes on for three months.
**State verbs** (*know, like, want, belong, understand*) describe a state, not an action → no -ing: *I **like** this dress* (not *am liking*).

examples.text: These days many students are learning to sew.
This month my aunt is staying with us in Dekemhare.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Why are you walking to school?" "My bicycle is broken, so I ____ this week."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "this week" and the broken bicycle show a temporary situation.

**Step 2:** Use the present continuous: am walking.

**Step 3:** The present simple would suggest a permanent habit.

**Tip:** am/is/are + -ing for now or around now (this week, these days). State verbs (know, like, want, belong) stay simple. accept = say yes to; except = not including; adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.

cards.title: Step by step: present continuous with a group word
cards.problem: Complete: "Listen! The national choir ____ (sing) the anthem in the main hall right now."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time words.** *Listen!* and *right now* = happening now → present continuous (am/is/are + -ing).
**Step 2: Find the subject.** *The choir* = one group → singular → **is**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I ________ the main reason for his sudden decision to leave the scholarship program.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *understand* is a **state verb**: it is about thinking, not an action.

**Step 2:** State verbs do not take -ing: ✗ *am understanding*.

**Step 3:** Subject *I* → **understand** (no -s). Answer: B.

**Tip:** State verbs (know, understand, like, want, believe, own) stay in the simple form: I understand, she knows.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Understand' (ምርዳእ) ሓደ ካብቶም ናይ ኣእምሮ ኩነታት ዝገልጹ ግሶች (state verbs) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቀጻሊ እዋን ክወስድ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ኣብ ትግርኛ 'ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ' (ቀጻሊ ዝመስል) እንተበልና እኳ፡ ብእንግሊዘኛ ግን ወትሩ 'understand' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና።

cards.title: Step by step: now, around now, or always?
cards.problem: Complete: (a) Look! Selam ____ (wear) a new zuria. (b) This term I ____ (take) extra maths lessons on Saturdays. (c) My father ____ (work) at the port in Massawa; he has worked there for years. (d) I ____ (like) your new shoes.

steps.text: **Step 2: Going on around now, for a limited period?** (b) *This term* → **am taking**.
**Step 3: Always true / a permanent job?** (c) → present simple **works**.

cards.answer: (a) is wearing (b) am taking (c) works (d) like

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: These days more and more young people in Asmara ____ online.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *These days* = a period around now, and a change that is happening.

**Step 2:** → present continuous: **are shopping**.

**Step 3:** *have shop* is not a correct form.

**Tip:** am/is/are + -ing for now or around now (this week, these days). State verbs (know, like, want, belong) stay simple. accept = say yes to; except = not including; adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.

cards.title: Confusing verbs
rule: **accept** = say yes to / agree to take (a verb): *accept a gift*. **except** = not including: *everyone **except** me*.
**adapt** = change to fit a new situation: *adapt to the hot climate of Massawa*. **adopt** = take as your own: *adopt a new style; adopt a child*.

examples.text: He adapted quickly to city life.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Everyone came accept Ruth."

steps.text: **Step 1: Know the two words.** *accept* = say yes to (a verb). *except* = not including.
**Step 2: Read the meaning.** Everyone came, but **not** Ruth → "not including".

body: acc**E**pt = **E**mbrace it; **EX**cept = **EX**clude it. ad**A**pt = **A**lter; ad**O**pt = **O**wn it.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: am / is / are + -ing = now or around now (this week, these days) and changes that are happening; state verbs stay simple. accept (say yes to) vs except (not including); adapt (change to fit) vs adopt (take as your own). have / has been + -ing = from the past up to now (how long).

cards.title: Step by step: Confusing verbs
body: **Step 1:** lie – lay – lain (no object after it: rest flat): "I lie down after lunch." lay – laid – laid (needs an object: put something down): "She laid the book on the table."
**Step 2:** rise – rose – risen (no object: go up): "The sun rises." raise – raised – raised (needs an object: lift): "Raise your hand."
**Step 3:** sit – sat – sat (no object) vs set – set – set (put something somewhere).
**Step 4:** say vs tell: say something (to someone); tell someone something: "He said that…", "He told me that…".
**Step 5:** borrow (take from someone) vs lend (give to someone); bring (towards the speaker) vs take (away from the speaker).
**Example:** "Yesterday the price of sugar (raised/rose)." → rose (no object). "Can you (borrow/lend) me your pen?" → lend. "She (said/told) me the answer." → told (a person follows).

cards.title: Mnemonic — "rAIse, lAY, sET take An object"
body: the verbs with the "a/e" sound before the object are the transitive ones.

cards.title: Exam tip
body: Ask "does the verb have an object right after it?" If yes, choose lay / raise / set / tell / lend; if no, choose lie / rise / sit / say.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Can I ____ your umbrella? I'll return it tomorrow."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The speaker wants to take and later return the umbrella.

**Step 2:** "borrow" = take for a time.

**Step 3:** "lend" would mean the speaker gives it.

**Tip:** am/is/are + -ing for now or around now (this week, these days). State verbs (know, like, want, belong) stay simple. accept = say yes to; except = not including; adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The temperature goes up by itself, with no object.

**Step 2:** Use "rise", which takes no object.

**Step 3:** Singular subject, general fact: rises.

**Tip:** am/is/are + -ing for now or around now (this week, these days). State verbs (know, like, want, belong) stay simple. accept = say yes to; except = not including; adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Don't ____ on the wet grass; you'll catch a cold."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The meaning is to rest your body flat, with no object.

**Step 2:** Use "lie".

**Step 3:** "lay" needs an object (lay the book).

**Tip:** am/is/are + -ing for now or around now (this week, these days). State verbs (know, like, want, belong) stay simple. accept = say yes to; except = not including; adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.

cards.title: Present perfect continuous: form and use
rule: **Form:** have/has + been + verb-ing. *I **have been waiting**. She **has been studying**.*
**Negative:** have/has + not + been + -ing: *They **haven't been sleeping** well.* **Question:** Have/Has + subject + been + -ing? ***Has** she **been working** here long?*
**Use 1 – it started in the past and is still going on now** (often with *for, since, How long…?*): *I **have been learning** English **for** six years.* *It **has been raining since** 8 o'clock.*
**Use 2 – it has just stopped and we can see the result now:** *Your eyes are red. **Have** you **been crying**?* *I'm hot because I**'ve been running**.*
**Use 3 – it happened again and again recently, up to now** (*recently, lately, these days*): *I**'ve been getting up** early **lately**.*
**for** + a period of time (*for two hours, for a week*); **since** + the starting point (*since Monday, since 2020, since I was ten*).
State verbs (*know, like, believe, own, understand*) do not take -ing: *I **have known** her for years* (not *have been knowing*).
**Not the past continuous:** *was/were + -ing* is for a moment in the **past** (*At 8 last night I **was reading***). *have been + -ing* reaches **now** (*I **have been reading** since 8*).

examples.text: She has been sewing dresses since this morning.
We have been waiting for the bus for forty minutes.
I am living in Keren since 2020.
examples.fix: I have been living in Keren since 2020.

examples.text: He has been knowing me for years.
examples.fix: He has known me for years.

examples.text: They have been work all day.
examples.fix: They have been working all day.

cards.title: Timeline: the action continues up to now
body: **PAST** ●———————————————→ **NOW** (and it may continue)
8:00 am – Selam starts sewing.  →  11:00 am (now) – she is still sewing.
**Selam has been sewing for three hours.** / **Selam has been sewing since 8 o'clock.**
The line starts in the past and reaches **now**. The present perfect continuous looks at the **whole line** and says **how long** it has lasted.
Compare: *Selam **is sewing**.* (only now) – *Selam **has been sewing** for three hours.* (from 8:00 until now)

cards.title: Present perfect or present perfect continuous?
head: Present perfect (have + V3)
Present perfect continuous (have been + -ing)
rows: the result: how much / how many
I have been writing letters all morning.
Maybe not finished: still going on, or just stopped.
I have known him for years. ✔
She has read the book. (she finished it)
She has been reading the book. (not finished yet)

cards.title: Link with Lesson 8.13: from "is doing" to "has been doing"
body: In Lesson 8.13 the writer of the job letter says: *Currently, I**'m attending** a three-month programme in secretarial science.* That is the **present continuous**: an action that goes on over a period around now.
Now ask **How long?** – *He started two months ago and he is still on the course.* → *He **has been attending** the programme **for two months**.* That is the **present perfect continuous**.
Your textbook uses it too: *So far you **have been writing** mainly individual paragraphs.* (Lesson 8.15, page 170) – the writing started in earlier lessons and goes on until now.
**Step 1:** Is the action still going on (or has it just stopped)? **Step 2:** Do you say how long (for / since / all day)? **Step 3:** Use **have/has + been + verb-ing**.

cards.title: When do we use it? Three uses
head: Use
Clue words
Example
rows: 1. It started in the past and is **still going on now**.
for, since, How long…?, all day, all morning
Aman **has been studying** for the matric exam **since September**.
2. It has **just stopped** and you can **see the result** now.
no time word; a result: tired, wet, dirty, red eyes
The road is wet. It **has been raining**.
3. It has happened **again and again** in the last days or weeks.
I**'ve been getting up** at 5 o'clock **lately** to study.

cards.title: Time words: for, since, How long, recently, all day
head: Word
What it means
Example
rows: a **length** of time: for two hours, for a week, for ten years, for a long time
We **have been waiting for** the bus **for** forty minutes.
the **starting point**: since 8 o'clock, since Monday, since 2020, since I was ten
Mr Tesfay **has been teaching** in Mendefera **since** 2015.
asks about the length: How long + have/has + subject + been + -ing?
**How long have** you **been living** in Dekemhare?
in the last few days or weeks (put it at the end)
The farmers **have been ploughing all morning**.
*ago* is a finished time → past simple, never *have been*
I **started** two hours **ago**. / I **have been working for** two hours.

cards.title: Side by side: three tenses that look alike
head: Present perfect continuous
Present perfect simple
Past continuous
rows: a past action with a result **now**
in progress **at a past moment** (it is finished now)
How many? How much? Is it done?
What was happening at that time?
Senait **has been cooking** since 6. (she is still cooking)
Senait **has cooked** three dishes. (they are ready – look!)
Senait **was cooking** at 6 yesterday. (that was yesterday)
My uncle **has been ploughing** the field all morning.
He **was ploughing** when it started to rain.
for, since, How long, all day, lately
already, yet, just, ever, never, so far, three times
at 8 last night, when…, while…, at that moment
Yes: still going on, or just stopped
No: it is about a past time

cards.title: Step by step: which of the three tenses?
cards.problem: Complete with has been + -ing, has + 3rd form, or was + -ing: (a) Look at Daniel's hands! He ____ (repair) bicycles all morning. (b) He ____ (repair) four bicycles so far. (c) At 10 o'clock yesterday he ____ (repair) my bicycle when the electricity went off. (d) How long ____ you ____ (wait) here? – Since 3 o'clock.

steps.text: **Step 1: Is it about a past moment that is finished?** (c) *At 10 o'clock yesterday … when the electricity went off* → yes → past continuous: **was repairing**.
**Step 2: Is there a number or a finished result?** (b) *four bicycles so far* → how many → present perfect simple: **has repaired**.
**Step 3: Is it an activity that lasted up to now (how long)?** (a) *all morning* + dirty hands now → **has been repairing**. (d) *How long … ? – Since 3 o'clock* → **have you been waiting**.
**Check the helper verb:** he/she/it → *has*; I/you/we/they → *have*; past continuous → *was/were*.

cards.answer: (a) has been repairing (b) has repaired (c) was repairing (d) have … been waiting

cards.title: Step by step: present perfect or present perfect continuous?
cards.problem: Complete: (a) Dawit ____ (play) football since 3 o'clock. He is very tired. (b) He ____ (score) two goals. (c) How long ____ you ____ (wait) for me? (d) I ____ (know) Ruth since primary school.

steps.text: **Step 1: Look for the clue words.** (a) *since 3 o'clock* + tired → an activity that has lasted until now. (b) *two goals* → a number = result. (c) *How long* → activity. (d) *know* → a state verb.
**Step 2: Activity + how long → have/has been + -ing.** (a) Dawit **has been playing**. (c) How long **have** you **been waiting**?
**Step 3: Result / number → have/has + V3.** (b) He **has scored** two goals.
**Step 4: State verb → never -ing.** (d) I **have known** Ruth since primary school.

cards.answer: (a) has been playing (b) has scored (c) have … been waiting (d) have known

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **HAVE BEEN + -ING = How long?** Ask *How long?* → have been + -ing. Ask *How many?* → have + V3.
**For** a period (*for 3 hours*), **since** a point (*since 3 o'clock*).

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: I am living in Keren since 2020.
I have been living in Keren since 2020.
From a past point up to now → have been + -ing, not am/is/are + -ing.
She has been teach here for years.
She has been teaching here for years.
He have been working all day.
He has been working all day.
I have been waiting since two hours.
I have been waiting for two hours.
A length of time → for; a starting point → since.
How long have you been waiting?
How long + up to now → have been + -ing.
I have been knowing her for years.
I have known her for years.
We have been visiting Massawa three times.
We have visited Massawa three times.
It rained yesterday. / It was raining yesterday.
A finished time (yesterday, ago) → past tense.

cards.title: State verbs: no -ing, so no present perfect continuous
head: Group
Verbs
Say this ✔
Not this ✘
rows: like, love, hate, want, need, prefer
She **has wanted** a bicycle for a long time.
My father **has had** this shop for 20 years.
My father has been having this shop…
I **have been** in Asmara for a week.
I have been being in Asmara…
have lunch, think about, see (= visit/meet)
I **have been thinking** about your idea. We**'ve been having** lunch.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: We ____ for the bus for forty minutes, and it still hasn't come.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *for forty minutes* + *it still hasn't come* → the waiting started in the past and is still going on.

**Step 2:** Use **have been + -ing**: *have been waiting*.

**Step 3:** *are waiting* does not show how long; *had waited* is past perfect.

**Tip:** for/since + still going on → present perfect continuous.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster ____ in this laboratory since she finished university five years ago.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *since she finished university* gives the starting point; she still works there.

**Step 2:** Started in the past + still true now → **has been working**.

**Step 3:** *is working* is a common mistake: English does not use the present continuous with *since*.

**Tip:** since + a starting point → have/has (been).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** We can see a result now (dirty hands) of an activity that has just stopped.

**Step 2:** Use the present perfect continuous: *What have you been doing?*

**Step 3:** *have you done* asks about a finished result, not the activity that made your hands dirty.

**Tip:** A visible result of a recent activity → have been + -ing.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I ____ three chapters of the book today.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *three chapters* is a number – the result.

**Step 2:** Result / how many → present perfect: **have read**.

**Step 3:** *have been read* is a passive form – wrong here.

**Tip:** How many? → have + V3. How long? → have been + -ing.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: I have been knowing Saba for ten years.
options.B: I know Saba since ten years.
options.C: I have known Saba for ten years.
options.D: I am knowing Saba for ten years.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** *know* is a state verb: no -ing.

**Step 2:** Started in the past and still true → present perfect: *have known*.

**Step 3:** *for* + a period (*ten years*), not *since*.

**Tip:** State verbs (know, like, own, believe) use the present perfect, not the continuous.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: When I phoned you at 8 o'clock last night, you ____ dinner.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *at 8 o'clock last night* is a moment in the past. It is finished now.

**Step 2:** An action in progress at a past moment → past continuous: **were having**.

**Step 3:** *have been having* would connect the action to **now** – but last night is not now.

**Tip:** Clue words: for / since / How long? / all day / lately → have been + -ing. How many? / a number / finished result → have + 3rd form. At a past moment (at 8 last night, when…) → was/were + -ing. Finished time (yesterday, ago) → past, never have been.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I'm tired. I ____ for the exam since 6 o'clock this morning.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *since 6 o'clock* = from a starting point up to now; *I'm tired* = we see the result now.

**Step 2:** An activity from the past up to now → **have been studying**.

**Step 3:** *was studying* is only about the past; *study* is a habit.

**Tip:** Clue words: for / since / How long? / all day / lately → have been + -ing. How many? / a number / finished result → have + 3rd form. At a past moment (at 8 last night, when…) → was/were + -ing. Finished time (yesterday, ago) → past, never have been.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: I have been owning this bicycle since 2022.
options.B: I have owned this bicycle since 2022.
options.C: I am owning this bicycle since 2022.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** *own* is a state verb: it never takes -ing.

**Step 2:** From 2022 until now → present perfect simple: **have owned**.

**Step 3:** *own … since* (present simple) is wrong: *since* needs have/has.

**Tip:** Clue words: for / since / How long? / all day / lately → have been + -ing. How many? / a number / finished result → have + 3rd form. At a past moment (at 8 last night, when…) → was/were + -ing. Finished time (yesterday, ago) → past, never have been.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Lately, my brother ____ to work by bus, because his car is broken.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *Lately* = again and again in the last days or weeks, up to now.

**Step 2:** A repeated activity up to now → **has been going**.

**Step 3:** *has gone* means one trip with a result (he is there now) – not a repeated activity.

**Tip:** Clue words: for / since / How long? / all day / lately → have been + -ing. How many? / a number / finished result → have + 3rd form. At a past moment (at 8 last night, when…) → was/were + -ing. Finished time (yesterday, ago) → past, never have been.

glossary.meaning: A verb for a state (thinking, feeling, having), not an action: know, like, want, belong. No -ing form.
have/has + been + verb-ing: an action that started in the past and is still going on (or has just stopped).
for + a period (for two hours); since + a starting point (since Monday).

tips.text: acc**E**pt = **E**mbrace it; **EX**cept = **EX**clude it. ad**A**pt = **A**lter; ad**O**pt = **O**wn it.
**How long?** → have been + -ing. **How many?** → have + V3.
**since / for / all day / lately → have been + -ing**, but **at 8 last night → was/were + -ing** and **three times → have + 3rd form**.
